scope: Static scene bounds category, dependency, region and sketch-context tracing; whole-scene provider admission remains unfinished.

native.mode: Retained static image only. No target execution, fresh target reads, native input, executable mapping or emulation.

findings: Ordered categories include mesh wrappers and point-cloud wrappers through separate iterator queries; general categories use the dependency-aware common collector followed by category classification.

The common collector resets its output, preserves order and duplicate entries, applies support/suppression/type exclusions, and conditionally applies visibility. Nonempty consumer lists accumulate higher-priority/nonexempt and consuming predicates independently; missing/unready/suppressed consumers retain the candidate.
Ordinary bounds screen their object predicate and excluded receiver, use special mesh/cloud cache branches, follow replacement-object bounds and perform an additional replacement-object pass.

An enabled transformed region builds bounds from eight corners, then intersects: source-operand MAXSS for lower bounds and MINSS for upper bounds. Its state also participates in an inclusive point-in-region predicate. UI flag ownership is not established.

Retained exact sketch-interface/type binding identifies the special source. Its stored records and child geometry contribute bounds; other scene bounds are transformed using the existing native rigid inverse and flattened to local XY. Invalid bounds expand to include the local minus-one to plus-one XY box.

The recovered inverse is already implemented and historically byte-tested as nativeDatumInverseFrame. Reuse it when binding the scene provider; do not introduce a generic inverse or duplicate arithmetic.
applicationImpact: These findings guide the still-gated scene provider. This evidence does not present a whole-scene adapter or native numerical runtime comparison as complete.
remaining: Bind category/type/cache/replacement and active-sketch source state to the application model.
